findings.title: Historical protocol promises across state replacement and recovery
findings.summary: This scenario tracks whether state replacement and recovery preserve protocol promises made before a replica lost volatile state. The involved paths include normal PrepareOk commit advancement, view change and StartView installation, same-view NewState installation, recovery response installation, install_log, and commit_up_to. The mechanism permits replacement of an uncommitted suffix while requiring any quorum-protected or already applied prefix to remain compatible across later views and incarnations. The model-checking source contains no covering candidate or counterexample for this run, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.

findings.title: Logical request identity, application replay, and reply reconstruction
findings.summary: This scenario tracks whether client-table rebuilding, committed execution, and cached replies describe the same sequential logical request history. Acceptance writes pending client entries, installation reconstructs latest client entries and selected cached replies, and execution applies committed log entries while conditionally caching results. Recovery may replay into the caller-supplied application without emitting recovery replies, while new-primary execution may emit replies. The model-checking source contains no covering candidate or counterexample for this run, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.

findings.title: Service and recovery progress under suitable timing
findings.summary: This scenario tracks whether retries, view changes, independent caller-driven clocks, and recovery response collection eventually complete work under the stated stable-service assumptions. The code paths include status-specific retry handling, capped timeout backoff, recovery quorum collection, and the simulator's synchronized idle and delivery schedule. The mechanism distinguishes client request completion from recovery completion and distinguishes finite DST convergence from a service progress guarantee. The model-checking source contains no covering candidate or counterexample for this run, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.

findings.title: Example obligations at the library boundary
findings.summary: This scenario tracks whether the shipped key-value example fulfills the library obligations for durability, client identity, recovery nonce freshness, timing, and transport delivery. The cited code includes blocking destination writes, view persistence, startup recovery, wall-time nonce generation, regular tick production through the main event queue, and persist-before-flush ordering. The mechanism is at the integration boundary: a conforming library caller can satisfy these assumptions, but the example still needs separate confirmation against its filesystem, timer, startup, identity, and queue behavior. The model-checking source contains no covering candidate or counterexample for this run, so this mechanism is retained as a code-review candidate for confirmation.
